too_fast.rule: a sentence (>= 4 s, >= 5 words) at or above p95 of comparable train sentences AND >= 25% faster than the speaker's usual sentence rate (p97 alone if no speaker baseline). Calibrated on train: the guide's p90 / +20% fired on 21% of answers
too_fast.rater_support: weak: faster speech goes with lower confidence scores within a participant (rho ~ -0.06) and lower scores between participants; the flag itself is not significant within participants (Stage 3). Describe, do not attribute the score to it.

too_slow.rule: mirror of too_fast: a sentence at or below p10 of comparable train sentences AND >= 20% slower than the speaker's usual. Was disabled on transcript words (Stage 1: 5/25 slowest sentences were transcript omissions); with verbatim ASR (Stage 4) the slowest sentences are real slow, hesitant speech (second ASR model agrees, low articulation rate), so it is back as EXPERIMENTAL until MIT / annotation show listeners hear it.
too_slow.rater_support: none (Stage 3: no within-participant relation; EBM shows no slow-side penalty)

rushed_opening.rule: first two sentences >= 20% faster than the rest AND the ratio above p90 of comparable answers (openings are faster than the rest in most answers: train median ratio ~1.14). EXPERIMENTAL since Stage 3: no relation with any rater score within participants
rushed_opening.rater_support: none (Stage 3 decision: drop for RecruitView; re-test on MIT / annotation)

hesitation.rule: longest mid-sentence pause >= max(1.0 s, p90 of comparable answers' longest mid-sentence pause) AND not shorter than the speaker's usual longest mid-sentence pause. EXPERIMENTAL since Stage 3: no within-participant relation, and between participants raters favour MORE pausing
hesitation.rater_support: none / contradicted between people (Stage 3); validate perceptually on MIT 'Paused' and the in-house annotation before any advice

long_answer.rule: speech span >= 2 x the train median for the same question type. Calibrated on train: the guide's 1.75 x fired on 19% of answers
long_answer.rater_support: weak but consistent: the same person's flagged answers get lower confidence and speaking-skills scores (within rho ~ -0.06); answer length is the only category whose within-participant relation survives in RecruitView (Stage 0 and 3)

slow_start.rule: silence before first speech above p90. EXPERIMENTAL: in RecruitView the clip start is not the end of the question, so this is not a true response latency

monotone.rule: pitch variability < p15 AND energy variability < p30 of comparable answers

trails_off.rule: >= 40% of sentences end > 6 dB lower than the speaker's usual end drop

uptalk.rule: >= 50% of sentences end with a rise >= 3 st over 300 ms (>= 10 st/s)

low_dominance.rule: answer dominance below p15 of comparable train answers AND its difference from the speaker's usual below p15 of train speaker differences (sounds less assured than other people AND than this speaker usually does); timestamp = lowest-dominance stretch
low_dominance.rater_support: contradicted: RecruitView raters score LOWER-dominance (calmer) speakers as more confident (between people rho -0.50); the flag has no within-person relation (Stage 3). Never advise 'sound more dominant'. Kept only for MIT validation.

tension_rise.rule: >= 6 s of consecutive windows with arousal AND pitch both > 1 SD above the speaker's usual (more activated and higher-pitched than this speaker in their other answers). Cannot tell tension from enthusiasm: the SER model's arousal and dominance correlate at 0.98 (Stage 5)
tension_rise.rater_support: weak but consistent: the same person's flagged answers get lower scores on all three targets (rho -0.06 to -0.07, CIs exclude 0; Stage 3), and more activated speakers score lower between people. Describe, do not attribute the score to it.

composure_drop.rule: the smoothed dominance curve falls by > 1 speaker SD within the answer AND the fall is above p90 of comparable answers (same length bucket: longer answers have more windows and larger maximum falls; > 1 SD alone fired on 70%); timestamp = from the peak to the low point
composure_drop.rater_support: none (Stage 3: no within-person relation); validate on MIT / annotation

notes.speaker_baseline: leave-one-out median of the same speaker's other recordings (copies excluded), >= 2 others; for a new user, the other segments of the same interview
notes.status: only 'active' flags/signals reach the evidence JSON; experimental ones are for Stage 3 validation; disabled ones are computed for monitoring only

pace.title: Pace & Rate Control
pace.note: Rates from verbatim ASR (Stage 4); slow answers are usually hesitant (pauses, filled pauses) rather than slowly articulated. Feedback on the slow side waits for MIT / annotation (no rater support yet).

pausing_fluency.title: Pausing & Fluency
pausing_fluency.note: Descriptive only: RecruitView raters reward more pausing between people and show no within-person penalty (Stage 3). Pauses classified by word boundaries (Stage 4); fillers are the text branch's. Validate against MIT 'Paused'.

expressiveness.title: Vocal Expressiveness
expressiveness.note: Pitch in semitones relative to the speaker; no RecruitView support yet (Stage 3). Validate against MIT 'EngagingTone'/'Excited' (Stage 7).

projection.title: Projection & Clarity
projection.note: Trailing off at real sentence ends (Stage 4; weak within-person support on all three scores). ASR word confidence was tested as intelligibility and rejected (opposite direction). Quality gate: Stage 6.

composure.title: Vocal Confidence & Composure
composure.note: Stage 5: vocal activation from a pretrained speech-emotion model (arousal; its dominance output is the same dimension here, rho 0.98), relative to the speaker's own other answers only (raw values are 87% speaker identity). Oriented by the RecruitView evidence: raters score CALMER speakers as more confident (between people rho -0.50; within a person weak, same direction). Describes how the voice sounded, never an inner state. Needs MIT 'Calm'/'NotStressed' (Stage 7) and a second SER model before feedback.

assertiveness.title: Assertive Delivery
assertiveness.note: Only sentence-final pitch movement for now; hedging phrases come from the text branch.

conciseness.title: Conciseness
conciseness.note: Relative to answers to the same question type. The only category whose relation with the ratings holds within the same person (Stages 0 and 3). 'Brief' is not flagged: very short answers are judged on content (text branch).
